biography: Michael Sandel is an American political philosopher whose work examines justice, markets, civic life, and the moral limits of human mastery. In The Case Against Perfection, he argues that genetic enhancement can threaten an attitude of giftedness: the capacity to receive parts of life as unchosen rather than treating every trait as a product to design. His objection is not reducible to safety or unequal access. PHIL 123 uses it to ask whether enhancement can change the meaning of achievement, responsibility, solidarity, and the goods of living with limits.

teaching.whyThisPerson: Sandel gives the enhancement debate a critique of mastery and asks what is lost when human capacities are treated entirely as design problems.
